courseDescription: TEMPORARY UNREVIEWED AI-GENERATED SAMPLE. English to Piedmontese, with one Lesson per current named Exercise type. The content is for testing and requires native-speaker review before language-teaching use. Basic spellings were checked against Claudio Panero's English-Piedmontese dictionary; examples and letter diagrams are newly authored. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontese voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.

content.text: Read the English source and pick its Piedmontese translation. ël can = the dog; ross = red; tre = three.
Pick the translation (to target): English to Piedmontese. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Note card — Good to know

content.text: Three notes about Piedmontese: the articles, the pronouns and the greetings.
Note card: Good to know. Three short examples use this exercise type.
Piedmontese has ël for masculine and la for feminine nouns; l' comes before a vowel: l'eva.
The subject pronoun is often doubled: mi i son means I am, literally me I am.
Bondì is good morning, bon-aneuit good night; ciàu works for hello and bye.
